name: Glucosylglycerol
description: Glucosylglycerol (CAS 22160-26-5 ) is a naturally occurring glycoside composed of glucose and glycerol, produced biotechnologically for commercial supply. Found in cyanobacteria and certain plants as an osmotic stress protectant, it functions industrially as a humectant. This skin-conditioning agent offers strong moisture-retention performance. In cosmetic formulations, it is used in serums, moisturizers, and leave-on treatments where it draws and retains water in the skin's upper layers. It supports hydration without the tackiness associated with glycerol at high concentrations. Its compatibility with sensitive-skin formulations makes it a preferred humectant in baby care and dermatological product lines. In food and nutraceutical applications, it is evaluated as a functional ingredient in hydration-focused beverages and dietary supplements. Pharmaceutical formulators also assess it as a stabilizing excipient for moisture-sensitive active ingredients. It is utilized in both topical and oral preparations. Glucosylglycerol is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations around 50% or higher, suited for direct incorporation into liquid formulations. Cosmetic-grade and food-grade designations are the most commercially relevant specifications available from established producers. Purity and grade documentation varies by supplier, so buyers should confirm specification sheets. Ensure that all documentation aligns with your specific regulatory and application requirements.
